title: Bayesian Distributional Models of Executive Functioning
abstract: arXiv:2510.00387v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This study uses controlled simulations with known ground-truth parameters to evaluate how Distributional Latent Variable Models (DLVM) and Bayesian Distributional Active LEarning (DALE) perform in comparison to conventional Independent Maximum Likelihood Estimation (IMLE). DLVM integrates observations across multiple executive function tasks and individuals, allowing parameter estimation even under sparse or incomplete data conditions. To establish known-ground truth, we uniformly sample individual sessions from a neural network learned latent space and map them to distributional cognitive performance across different tasks. The individual test-items are then sampled from these distributions using either DALE, random procedure or a standard fixed battery approach. translated_title: 执行功能的贝叶斯分布模型
translated_abstract: 本研究使用已知真实参数的受控模拟，评估了分布潜变量模型（DLVM）和贝叶斯分布主动学习（DALE）与传统独立最大似然估计（IMLE）相比的性能。DLVM整合了多个执行功能任务和个体间的观测，即使在稀疏或不完整的数据条件下也能进行参数估计。为了建立已知的真实值，我们从神经网络学习的潜空间中均匀采样个体会话，并将其映射到不同任务上的分布性认知表现。随后，使用DALE、随机程序或标准固定电池方法从这些分布中采样个体测试项目。在给定相同观测集的情况下，DLVM始终优于IMLE，尤其是在数据量较少时，并能更快地收敛到高度准确的估计。
tldr: 本研究通过模拟验证了DLVM在稀疏数据下比传统IMLE更准确且收敛更快，并展示了DALE在采样中的优势。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that DLVM outperforms traditional IMLE in accuracy and convergence speed under sparse data, highlighting DALE's advantage in sampling.
